title: Handling personal and confidential data
summary: How data in the data warehouse is classified, who may see it, how long it is kept, and where personal data must never end up.
scope: All datasets in the data warehouse and the code that loads or queries them. Operational databases of applications follow the standard of their platform.

resources.title: Privacy notice for customers
resources.description: What we promised customers about their data.

requirements.title: Every dataset is classified
requirements.statement: Every dataset carries a classification label - public, internal, confidential or personal - set to the highest class of the data in it.
requirements.rationale: Access, retention and masking rules all follow from the class. Without a label nobody knows which rules apply.
guidance: Classify the columns when you request the dataset.
Raise the label as soon as a more sensitive column is added.

verification.description: Nightly check for datasets without a classification label.

requirements.title: Personal data only after a privacy check
requirements.statement: Personal data is loaded into the warehouse only for a purpose the data protection officer has checked, and only the columns that purpose needs.
requirements.rationale: The law allows personal data to be used only for a stated purpose and only as much as needed.
guidance: Ask for the privacy check in the dataset request.
Replace names and emails with a hashed customer id where the purpose allows it.

verification.description: Privacy check in the dataset request and the yearly data audit.

requirements.title: No real personal data outside production
requirements.statement: Development and test datasets contain no real personal data; use generated or masked data.
requirements.rationale: Development and test environments are open to many more people and tools than production.
guidance: Use the masked copy job to fill test datasets.
Generate test customers with the data faker library.

verification.description: A scanner samples development and test datasets for real email addresses and phone numbers.

lookFor: A job that copies a production dataset to a development or test project without masking
Test data files with real-looking names, emails or phone numbers

requirements.title: Keep data only as long as needed
requirements.statement: Tables with personal or confidential data have an expiry that matches the retention period agreed for the dataset.
requirements.rationale: Data that is kept for ever is a risk for ever.
guidance: Set the default table expiry on the dataset.
For partitioned tables, set the partition expiry.

verification.description: Weekly report of personal datasets without an expiry.

requirements.title: Select the columns you need
requirements.statement: Queries and views on personal datasets name the columns they need instead of selecting everything.
requirements.rationale: SELECT * copies personal columns into reports and extracts that never needed them.
guidance: List the columns in every query that feeds a report or an export.

lookFor: SELECT * on a table in a personal or confidential dataset

requirements.title: No local copies of personal data
requirements.statement: Notebooks and scripts work on personal data inside the warehouse and do not write it to local files or spreadsheets.
requirements.rationale: Local files are not covered by the warehouse's access control, expiry or audit log.
guidance: Aggregate in BigQuery and download only the result.
Use a hashed id instead of a name in anything you export.

lookFor: to_csv, to_excel or open(..., 'w') on a data frame read from a personal dataset
